related_questions.question: Is there a virus that makes you dizzy?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, viral infections can cause dizziness. Specifically, viral infections can lead to conditions like vestibular neuritis and labyrinthitis, which are characterized by vertigo (a spinning sensation) and other symptoms like dizziness, imbalance, and nausea. These conditions often follow a cold or flu. COVID-19 has also been linked to dizziness, both during and after the infection.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, viral infections can cause dizziness

list.title: Vestibular Neuritis and Labyrinthitis:
list.snippet: These inner ear disorders are often caused by viral infections. Vestibular neuritis affects the vestibular nerve, while labyrinthitis involves inflammation of the inner ear. Symptoms include sudden, severe vertigo, dizziness, imbalance, and nausea.

list.title: Flu and Other Viruses:
list.snippet: The flu (influenza), herpes viruses (like chickenpox and shingles), and other viruses can trigger vestibular neuritis and labyrinthitis.

list.title: COVID-19:
list.snippet: COVID-19 can cause dizziness, both during the active infection and as a lingering symptom (long COVID). In some cases, it's been linked to Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), which can cause dizziness upon standing.

list.title: Other Causes:
list.snippet: While viral infections are a common cause, other factors can also lead to dizziness, including benign positional vertigo and Meniere's disease.

text_blocks.snippet: If you're experiencing dizziness, especially if it's severe or accompanied by other symptoms, it's best to consult with a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.
